title: 16lwti6
Imam Hasan, the peace treaty and Umayyad rule
hook: Imam Hasan, whom the Prophet called a sayyid, gave up his right so that the blood of the community would not be shed, and he was poisoned.
scenes.0.text: One day the Prophet was speaking on the pulpit. His little grandson Imam Hasan was beside him. The Prophet loved him dearly. He kept looking at the congregation, and then at him.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.0.art.actors.2.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.1.text: On the pulpit, beside Imam Hasan, the Prophet said: "This son of mine is a sayyid. Through him God will reconcile two great groups of Muslims." Years later this glad tidings was fulfilled in the peace treaty.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.2.text: In Medina, in **the Prophet's Mosque**, the congregation had lined up for prayer. The Prophet came into the mosque carrying one of his grandsons. The Companion **Shaddad b. al-Had** relates that the child in his arms that day was **Imam Hasan** or **Imam Husayn**. The Prophet set the child down beside him, said the takbir and began the prayer. When he went into prostration, the little grandson climbed onto his back. The Prophet did not lift his head from the ground and made the prostration far longer than usual. When Shaddad raised his head in curiosity, he saw the child on the Prophet's back and went back down into prostration. When the prayer ended, the people said, "O Messenger of God, you prolonged the prostration so much that we thought something had happened or that revelation was coming to you." The Prophet answered: "None of that happened. My son climbed onto my back. I did not want to hurry him until he had finished." **Abu Hurayra** also describes a night (isha) prayer. That night, each time the Prophet prostrated, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn leapt onto his back. When he raised his head, he took them gently from behind with his hand and set them down. When he prostrated again, the two brothers climbed onto his back once more. After the prayer he sat them on his lap. When Abu Hurayra offered to take the children to their mother, a flash of lightning lit the sky. The Prophet told them, "Go to your mother." The two brothers walked in the light of the lightning until they reached **Lady Fatima**. Shia sources also report that the Prophet prolonged his prostration while Imam Hasan was on his shoulder and said, "My son was on my shoulder, and I did not want to hurry him until he came down."
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.2.art.actors.2.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.2.art.actors.3.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.3.text: In Ramadan 40 Imam Ali was martyred. The people of Kufa gave their pledge of allegiance to his son Imam Hasan. Pledge (bay'a) means a word of allegiance. Imam Hasan became the new leader of the believers. The duty his father had left was now his.
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.4.text: In Damascus, **Mu'awiya** held the trade routes in his hands. He was very wealthy. He marched on Kufa with his army. The two sides drew near each other. There was the danger of a new civil war.
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.5.text: **Mu'awiya** bought **Imam Hasan**'s commanders with deceit, purchase and bribery. **Ubaydullah b. Abbas** left the army at night and went over to **Mu'awiya**. The army rotted from within. **Imam Hasan** was left powerless. So that blood would not be shed and the friends of the ==Ahl al-Bayt== would not be broken, he ended the war. Rule passed to **Mu'awiya**. This year is called 'Am al-Jama'a. It means the year of unity.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.6.text: The agreement was put in writing. **Imam Hasan** did not give up his right. **Mu'awiya** was to act according to the Book of God, not to have anyone cursed, and not to appoint a caliph after himself. He later ==broke== these conditions. **Imam Ali** was cursed from the pulpits.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.7.text: After the peace treaty **Imam Hasan** left Kufa and returned to Medina. There, in his grandfather's city, he lived a quiet life for about ten years. **Mu'awiya**, however, wanted to make his son **Yazid** caliph after him. The greatest obstacle on that path was Imam Hasan, who knew the terms of the treaty and carried the love of the people. Mu'awiya secretly sent word to Imam Hasan's wife **Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath**. He promised that if she poisoned Imam Hasan, he would marry her to his son Yazid and give her a hundred thousand dirhams. Ja'da was taken in by this promise and gave her husband the poison Mu'awiya had sent. Imam Hasan suffered for about forty days and then passed away. His death is given as 28 Safar 49 or 50. According to a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the one who poisoned Imam Hasan was Ja'da. When Imam Hasan was martyred, Mu'awiya did not keep his word. Ja'da neither married Yazid nor received all of the promised money. In this way the last obstacle before Yazid's succession was removed by Mu'awiya's hand.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.8.text: Imam Hasan left a will to his family. He asked to be buried beside his grandfather, the Messenger of God. "Let not a drop of blood be shed at my funeral," he said. If blood was to be shed, he told them to bury him in al-Baqi', beside his mother.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.8.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.9.text: **Imam Husayn** and the Banu Hashim lifted Imam Hasan's coffin onto their shoulders and walked toward the Prophet's grave. At that very moment **Aisha**, riding a mule, blocked the way together with **Marwan** and the Umayyads. She did not allow the coffin to be buried beside the Prophet. Marwan too shouted, "While Uthman is buried in al-Baqi, is Hasan to be buried in the Prophet's house?" On Aisha's order, arrows were shot at the coffin of the Prophet's grandson. Seeing this, **Ibn Abbas** could not hold back and said to Aisha: "One day you ride a camel, one day a mule." At the Camel she had ridden a camel against Imam Ali, and now she had ridden a mule against Imam Hasan's funeral.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: sbbh7k
Marwan
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.9.art.actors.2.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.10.text: Marwan's men shot arrows at Imam Hasan's coffin on Aisha's order. The arrows stuck in the coffin. Al-Dinawari attributes the arrows to the Umayyads. Ibn Shahrashub says seventy arrows. This number rests on a single source.
scenes.10.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.11.text: Imam Husayn did not draw his sword. His brother had a will: "Let not a drop of blood be shed at my funeral." Imam Hasan was buried in al-Baqi'. His grave is beside that of his grandmother Fatima bint Asad.
scenes.11.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.12.text: When **Mu'awiya** died in 60, he left the throne to his son **Yazid**. The caliphate now remained within one family. Imam Husayn did not pledge allegiance to Yazid. The end of this sultanate was Karbala.
scenes.12.art.actors.0.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.12.art.actors.2.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
sunni.0.says: From Abu Bakra: The Prophet, on the pulpit with Imam Hasan beside him, says, "This son of mine is a sayyid; through him God will reconcile two great groups of Muslims." The report also tells of Imam Hasan's peace treaty with Mu'awiya.
sunni.1.says: A repetition of the same Abu Bakra report in other chapters is to be expected.
sunni.2.says: From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn are the masters of the youth of Paradise.
sunni.3.says: The pledge of allegiance to Imam Hasan after Imam Ali's martyrdom, the confrontation with Mu'awiya and the handing over of rule.
sunni.4.says: That Imam Hasan was buried in al-Baqi' and a great crowd gathered at the funeral; it does not contain the matter of burial beside the Prophet and the obstruction.
sunni.4.grade: al-Waqidi is in the chain; generally regarded as weak by hadith scholars
sunni.5.says: It is reported that Aisha initially agreed to Imam Hasan's wish to be buried beside the Prophet.
sunni.6.says: Marwan's saying, "While Uthman is buried in al-Baqi', is Hasan to be buried in the Prophet's house?"
sunni.7.says: The account of Marwan's informing Mu'awiya and of the demands about the burial place.
sunni.8.says: The report that Aisha came on a mule and wanted the Hashimites to be prevented.
sunni.9.says: That the Umayyads shot arrows at Imam Hasan's funeral.
sunni.10.says: It is relayed "according to the report" that Ja'da was persuaded by the promise of marriage to Yazid and poisoned Imam Hasan.
sunni.11.says: He relays the account of the poisoning (the physician's saying that the intestines were torn to pieces, Imam Husayn's question "who did it?"), but rejects the report of Yazid's promise to Ja'da, saying "in my view it is not authentic, and even more remote in the case of Mu'awiya."
sunni.12.says: He says that it is not established by reliable evidence that Mu'awiya had him poisoned, and that speaking on this matter would be speaking without knowledge.
sunni.13.says: It is relayed that some early Sunni historians (according to Madelung) attributed the poison to Mu'awiya; that al-Waqidi attributed the poison to a servant acting on Mu'awiya's behalf.
sunni.14.says: From Shaddad b. al-Had: the Prophet came to prayer carrying Imam Hasan or Imam Husayn and prolonged the prostration; when asked, he said, "My son climbed onto my back, and I did not want to hurry him until he had finished."
sunni.15.says: A parallel of Shaddad's report; and from Abu Hurayra: at the isha prayer, when the Prophet prostrated, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn would leap onto his back and he would set them down gently; after the prayer he sat them on his lap, and when lightning flashed he said, "Go to your mother."
sunni.15.grade: Editors: chain of 16033 sahih, chain of 10659 hasan
sunni.16.says: Abu Hurayra's report of the isha prayer: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn leap onto the Prophet's back in prostration, and after the prayer they go to their mother in the light of the lightning.
shia.0.says: The pledge of allegiance to Imam Hasan, the peace treaty with Mu'awiya, and the report that Imam Hasan died by poisoning.
shia.1.says: The blocking of the way, Imam Husayn's prevention of bloodshed, and Imam Hasan's burial beside his grandmother; Marwan's words.
shia.2.says: That arrows were shot at the funeral and seventy arrows struck; this detail has been found only in this source.
shia.3.says: The tension over the burial and Imam Hasan's will.
shia.4.says: The report that Imam Hasan said in advance that Aisha would obstruct.
shia.5.says: That Mu'awiya came to an agreement with Ja'da and had Imam Hasan poisoned with the promise of money and marriage to Yazid; that the death occurred about forty days later.
shia.6.says: From Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq: The one who poisoned Imam Hasan is Ja'da.
shia.7.says: According to some reports, Mu'awiya gave the poison to Ja'da.
shia.8.says: The saying attributed to Mu'awiya, "I fear that you will do to my son what you did to the son of the Prophet with poison." Who said it to whom, and its authenticity, were not verified.
shia.9.says: It is related that Imam Husayn took his brother to the Messenger of God, that Aisha came on a mule and herself prevented the coffin from being buried there and gave the order for arrows, that Marwan's men shot at the coffin with this order, Ibn Abbas's saying "one day the camel, one day the mule," and that, according to Imam Hasan's will that blood not be shed, he was buried in al-Baqi'. The page number was not given separately.
shia.10.says: It is related that Mu'awiya had Imam Hasan poisoned by promising Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath marriage to Yazid and a hundred thousand dirhams, and that he did not keep his promise. The page number was not given separately.
shia.11.says: When the Prophet prolonged his prostration, Imam Hasan was on his shoulder; he said, "Revelation did not come to me; my son was on my shoulder, and I did not want to hurry him until he came down." The words "my son climbed onto my back" from Shaddad's report are also relayed.
disputes.0.title: 143aevt
How is the peace treaty read?
disputes.0.sunni: It is told that through Imam Hasan's peace treaty two groups were reconciled. This event also appears in Sunni sources (al-Bukhari, No. 2704). In the Sunni reading, this is his virtue and the unity of the community.
disputes.0.shia: It is told that through Imam Hasan's peace treaty two groups were reconciled. This event also appears in Sunni sources (al-Bukhari, No. 2704). In the Shia account, he did not give up his right, and the conditions were broken afterwards.
disputes.1.title: 1jf3g0w
Who poisoned Imam Hasan?
disputes.1.sunni: That Imam Hasan was poisoned appears in many sources, and Ja'da's name is mentioned. Ibn Taymiyya and Ibn Kathir say that Mu'awiya's order is not established by authentic evidence.
disputes.1.shia: That Imam Hasan was poisoned appears in many sources, and Ja'da's name is mentioned. In Shia books Mu'awiya is held to have had him poisoned for Yazid's path; Imam Hasan is a martyr.
disputes.2.title: 19ofwqm
Why was the burial not beside the Prophet?
disputes.2.sunni: It is told that Imam Hasan wished to be buried beside the Prophet. In the Sunni reading the room was at Aisha's disposal; there was concern about strife (fitna), and it is stressed that the real objection came from Marwan.
disputes.2.shia: It is told that Imam Hasan wished to be buried beside the Prophet. In the Shia account, Aisha herself prevented the coffin from being buried beside the Prophet and gave the order for arrows. Marwan's men shot with this order. Imam Husayn did not draw his sword because of the will that blood not be shed.
disputes.3.title: 19r0ddp
Who shot the arrows?
disputes.3.sunni: That arrows were shot at the funeral is attributed to the Umayyads in al-Dinawari. The arrows were shot by Marwan's men. That Aisha herself obstructed and gave the order for arrows is in the Shia report (al-Irshad, Bihar; the page number was not given separately).
disputes.3.shia: Aisha gave the order for arrows. Marwan's men shot at the coffin, and the arrows stuck in the coffin. Ibn Shahrashub says seventy arrows; this number rests on a single source.
disputes.4.title: 88iswv
The masters of the youth of Paradise
disputes.4.sunni: That Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn are called the masters of the youth of Paradise is a great virtue. This event also appears in Sunni sources (al-Tirmidhi, No. 3768). In the Sunni reading, no ruling of imamate is drawn from this saying.
disputes.4.shia: That Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn are called the masters of the youth of Paradise is a great virtue. This event also appears in Sunni sources (al-Tirmidhi, No. 3768). In the Shia account, this saying is mentioned together with the spiritual leadership of the Ahl al-Bayt.
questions.0: Most early sources report that Imam Hasan was poisoned. What kind of sorrow and what questions does the death of this grandson, who gave up rule for the sake of peace, leave within you?
questions.1: Imam Hasan wished to be buried beside his grandfather, the Prophet. What do this wish and the obstacle before it tell you?
questions.2: It is reported that tension arose during the funeral and that arrows were shot. Imam Husayn held back so that blood would not be shed. What does this patience teach you?
questions.3: The Prophet called Imam Hasan a sayyid and announced that he would reconcile two groups. What do you feel about a grandson who chose to stop the bloodshed?
questions.4: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn had been called the masters of the youth of Paradise. How do the later years of the two brothers lead you to read this love?
questions.5: The terms of the peace treaty and the death are told differently in the books. In such a place, which account would you trust, and why?
questions.6: While Imam Hasan gave up rule for the sake of peace, in the next generation rule passed from father to son. What does this change tell you about understanding Imam Husayn's stand?
summary: Imam Hasan, whom the Prophet called a sayyid, received the pledge of allegiance after his father's martyrdom. When Mu'awiya bought the army with bribes, he ended the war so that blood would not be shed. The terms of the treaty were later broken. About ten years later he died, poisoned.
notes.0: The Prophet said of Imam Hasan, «this son of mine is a sayyid» (al-Bukhari 2704).
notes.1: After Imam Ali's martyrdom, the pledge of allegiance was given to Imam Hasan.
notes.2: After the army was bought, he ended the war so that blood would not be shed. Rule passed to Mu'awiya. The terms of the treaty were later broken. This year was called the «year of unity.»
notes.3: He lived in Medina for about ten years and died, poisoned.
notes.4: Imam Hasan died by poisoning; this is also told in history books. In the Ja'fari school he is a martyr.
notes.5: At the funeral, Aisha herself prevented the coffin from being buried beside the Prophet and gave the order for arrows. Marwan's men shot at the coffin. Imam Husayn did not draw his sword. Imam Hasan was buried in al-Baqi' (al-Irshad, Bihar).
